verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The paper's single display is two Lean statements that conjoin in one line. (a) Factorization: `pairMatrix_factorization` gives H i j = (pairScales …) j * (normalizedPair P) i j, which is H_σ = h_σ · (unit-mass direction) with h_σ exactly the scalar of eq-p083-1. (b) Direction: setting e_σ := normalizedPair P (·,σ) − H0 (·,σ), `normalizedPair_entry_error` bounds |e_σ| ≤ (E + D·concentrationConstant)/r; at H0 = `signedModel c₀ u` (used so in `PulseCovariance.compact_actual_positive_inverse`, line 747, via `normalizedMatrix_entry_error`) the column σ of signedModel is ![c₀√(1+u_*²), −σu_*], and with A_c = −c₀√(1+u_*²) that is −A_c N − σ u_* K, matching the paper's signs and the N/K components. (c) Rate: the Lean bound is C/r, and r² = L_s (`slotRadius_sq`) with L_s ≍ S_* in the chart (`chart_length_identity`, `chart_scalar_factor_bounds`, PrimaryCovarianceBounds.lean:177 and :181), so C/r = C L_s^{-1/2} ≍ C S_*^{-1/2} — the paper's rate. What the Lean leaves as an explicit hypothesis rather than a conclusion is the paper's input sentence 'by Lemma 7.4, its ratio to x differs by O(S_*^{-1}) from −s(v)K + c₀√(1+s(v)²)N': it appears as `hratio : |t v i / x v − H0 i j| ≤ E/r² + D|v − r²/2|/r²`, with the affine drift of s(v) carried by the D-term (`PulseCovariance.affineSlope`, `modelDirection_affine_drift`).
